q: Being a first time mum who I must admit hadn’t looked into induction at all, I simply went with the doctors recommendation.
cx: Eight weeks into a second pregnancy, UK, looking back at an unprepared first induction.
r: previous-birth injury and emergency, procedure decision

q: I feel like we completely lost all trust in the midwives that day (the surgeons on the other hand, who saved my life, I still trust impeccably).
cx: Why her second pregnancy starts with dread.

q: since it’s being the holidays I am noticing it a lot more with being up on my feet with my toddler
cx: 35 weeks in the UK, summer holidays with her 5-year-old.
r: medical condition (anaemia) in the same passage

q: I’ve mentioned I wanted to quit, but lactation consultants, my partner, doctors all want me to stick to it because of the health benefits and it’s best for the baby. I’ve been told formula is nasty, the smell and the texture.
cx: Three weeks after the birth, pumping through pain.

q: I can’t go out without packing coolers for milk, my pump, all of the parts, a change of clothes in case I spill milk everywhere. If I go out longer than 3 hours it’s like a major sporting event.
cx: What pumping does to leaving the house at three weeks postpartum.

q: I’m miserable and can’t imagine feeling this way for several more weeks until I hit my second trimester.
cx: Eight weeks, constant nausea, counting down to the second trimester.

q: it seemed to me that the expectation when she announced her wedding date was that of course I’d be able to attend as it’s a few weeks out and I could just drop the baby off with my parents.
cx: A friend's child-free wedding falls 5-6 weeks after her first due date.

q: I can’t foresee myself having fun knowing I have to leave my baby - I also feel nervous driving up there on my own (not that experienced driving) since my husband would stay with baby
cx: Why she is leaning to a firm no to the wedding.

q: at A&E I’m literally saying to them “it’s just piles. I don’t need to be seen” while my colleague is being dramatic going “but your placenta! Your baby! You need checking”- again it was just humiliating.
cx: UK; triage told her to see her GP, but a colleague insisted on A&E.

q: I’ve been sent home from work early, as my management want me to still go to a walk in and get checked
cx: The end of the afternoon at work.

q: but i am alone and i am scared. happy somewhat, but mostly scared. my mom died 4 years ago and i don’t have any female friends with kids. so i don’t even know the first […] thing about anything.
cx: Just found out at 5-6 weeks, 33, single, on holiday.

q:
I'm pregnant and setting up my nursery, and every device we buy comes with its own app... I already get confused with the wiz and wyze app (philips smart lamps and security cameras)

And now the baby monitor came with its own app (momcozy), and the Dreamegg sound machine/night light came with yet another one (tuya) 😂
cx: A pregnant woman asks dads how to put all the nursery gadgets in one app.

q: I have a feeling I'm going to lose my mind trying to keep track of all of these during the postpartum period 🫠
cx: Same post: nursery gadget apps.

q: With a nesting shopping list so big, I'm bound to get whatever is on sale or make it work with items I got on my baby shower hehe
cx: Why her nursery gadgets don't match one ecosystem.

q: I requested to go part time as my commute is becoming too much for me but that’s denied as we don’t have my replacement yet.
cx: 16 weeks, first baby, burnt out at a short-staffed job she won't return to.

q: My husband gave me his blessing to quit and enter my SAHM era early but I’m totally guilt tripping myself because most moms work at least until 30 weeks and here I am complaining at 16 😅
cx: Same post; she measures herself against other mothers working on.

q: I do not feel safe bringing a child into this world with my place like this and idk what to do. I haven’t slept these couple of days and I’m on the verge of crying.
cx: Two weeks before a scheduled induction, a burst pipe leaves her rented home with holes and wet carpet.

q: My sister in law told me she felt “euphoric” after giving birth and with her newborns.
cx: First-time mother, five days after the birth, scared by mood shifts.

q: He takes care of me so I can take care of her. He makes sure I sleep and reminds me 24/7 how much he loves me and is so proud of me.
cx: Contrary voice: a partner who carries the first days.

q: I'm feeling a lot of pressure from people when researching online to breastfeed when the time comes, and it's making me feel guilty and overwhelmed.
cx: Nine weeks, already planning how she will feed.
